recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core follow-up is needed for FHIR-14378; future capabilitystatement-expectation cardinality or context work should be made in HL7/fhir-extensions, with core updating only external references if their target changes.
issue_request: FHIR-14378 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core issue asking to relax the capabilitystatement-expectation extension root cardinality from 1..1 to 0..1 for R4 and future releases so profiles could introduce the extension without making every use mandatory.
initial_application: Core commit 0016b634322d6d6ee5ca6913153aaf3b6c91bd5d, matching the Jira comment's svn revision 13416, changed the old source/capabilitystatement/capabilitystatement-extensions-spreadsheet.xml row for capabilitystatement-expectation from 1..1 to 0..1. R4 and R4B checked-in history bundles show Extension min 0 and max 1.
additional_context: The STU3 history bundle still reflects the published STU3 1..1 definition, which is consistent with the Jira text saying NHS Digital would copy the extension for STU3 and asking HL7 to relax the official extension for R4/future. The current FHIR-core checkout no longer has an active profile source for capabilitystatement-expectation; core pages link through the external extension-location mechanism, and the current Extension Pack source defines the extension root as 0..1.
reconciliation: No FHIR-core source change was made. The issue was recorded with an empty external-repo audit commit on the combined branch because the current core checkout is not the authoritative source for the extension definition and the external authoritative source already has the requested cardinality.
source_changes: No FHIR-core source files changed; empty external-repo audit commit only.
